data:
GWRHelp: Ready. Set. GO!!!!!!! 
Check out the acceleration of Great Western Railway's new Intercity Express Train compared to a High Speed Train as it leaves Chippenham station. This is one of the ways that the train will reduce journey times once they are all in service in 2019. https://t.co/dj4ihloZQU
Customer: @GWRHelp How much quicker will a journey between Paddington and Penzance be?
Customer: @GWRHelp Just hope everyone gets a seat though!  Bristol to Portsmouth train recently was like Tube in rush hour...
GWRHelp: @790972 Hi. The 802s will operate between London Paddington and Penzance. The journey time will be up to 16 minutes quicker. Lewis
Customer: @GWRHelp Thank you for this. Could you do a similar comparison of the top speed of the two types on diesel, say up Dauntsey Bank?
GWRHelp: @275743 We will record your feedback. They are both under diesel and that video is at Chippenham station with electric wires. :) Rachel
Customer: @GWRHelp Good to see the speed change for the IET over the HST. IET made of 2 'trains', what is the plan regarding buffet car/food?
Customer: @524048 @GWRHelp It always is clare .. they could do with putting some hst sets on that route , even if only 5?car sets which is minimum for breaking
Customer: @GWRHelp @790972 But three times more expensive!
Customer: @GWRHelp Thanks. Not exactly ground breaking 😂 I hope the seats are more comfortable for long distance than current HST.
Customer: @GWRHelp Nice to see that there's finally a compared video! These 800s are truly fantastic units! Need to bag a trip from BRI to SWI soon!
GWRHelp: @275743 *without electric wires. Apologies.
Customer: @484651 @GWRHelp Oh dear...I’m heading that way again soon #sardines such a shame as a beautiful route
GWRHelp: @790966 Hi Michael, there will be an at seat trolley service in First and Standard class in each five car unit. -Andy
GWRHelp: @320096 Glad you like it. We look forward to welcoming you on this service soon! Rachel
Customer: @GWRHelp Thanks Andy. Now I just need to wait for them to reach Cornwall
Customer: @GWRHelp Shame that most trips are to South Wales at the moment!
Customer: @GWRHelp The new trains are cramped and claustrophobic compared to the old trains. A step backwards in comfort....
GWRHelp: @790966 Not too much longer, will start to run on that route from next summer. -Andy
GWRHelp: @790965 Hi Simon, sorry you're unhappy with the on board comfort the seats are ergonomically designed and provide more legroom per seat as well as more seats per carriage. -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp Meanwhile back in reality the 1706 is cancelled adding 45 minutes to my journey home, thanks!
GWRHelp: @790958 Hi Simon, sorry to hear this. The 17:06 from where to where? -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp Thanks. My observation is that the new trains struggle to do much more than 115 mph uphill on diesel while the old HSTs easily achieve line speed of 125.
Customer: @GWRHelp This is on a non  electrified part of the railway ?  Will it be faster on an electrified part of the the railway?
Customer: @GWRHelp PAD to THA although I notice you were quick enough to add an extra stop at Twyford on the 1703 Penzance service. Lucky them!
Customer: @GWRHelp When will the new trains be stopping at Maidenhead into Paddington? Thanks.
Customer: @GWRHelp And will the cost of travel reduce?
GWRHelp: @790960 Hello, yes the acceleration will be even greater under electric power. -Andy
GWRHelp: @360970 Hi Dan, Maidenhead already has new electric commuter trains but the IETs will start replacing the HSTs on this route from next year as more are delivered to us. -Andy
GWRHelp: @391823 Hi Andrew, fares won't change as a result of the new trains. -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp In short then, they will change, but only to increase
Customer: @GWRHelp @272023 Well ya not going to show a hst beating a new train are you. See what the class800 is like in 40 yrs, if they havnt fell to bits by then.
GWRHelp: @790958 Additional stops will be made if operationally possible and if the demand is there. Apologies for the cancellation this evening, this is due to an earlier broken down train.  Rachel
GWRHelp: @391823 Regulated fares do rise each year, usually not above the Retail Price Index. -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp @272023 I have travelled on both and can compare- class800 very uncumfy. Hst- certainly more cumfy.
GWRHelp: @426690 @272023 Thanks for the feedback Jed. All feedback is recorded and noted. Rachel
Customer: @GWRHelp @272023 Ya welcome
Customer: @GWRHelp You should see it on Electric! Never mind racing a HST, it beats a 387!
Customer: @GWRHelp Will the train crews bother to turn up for this new train or will it be the same old same old?
GWRHelp: @364001 Maybe we'll do some more videos then! -Andy
Customer: @426690 @GWRHelp @272023 I have just done a pair from Cardiff to Paddington and back. They absolutely flew.
Customer: @GWRHelp @790958 I had a demand to catch the 17:03 (to Newbury) but I missed it, as you took it off the screens early (apparently due to overcrowding).  Presumably, it wouldn't have been overcrowded had the Twyford crowd been forced to catch one of the five services available to them before 6pm?
GWRHelp: @791439 @426690 @272023 Glad you like #GWRNewTrains Neil! More coming soon and even faster from 2019. -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp Great - but when will these trains actually be stopping at Maidenhead please?
GWRHelp: @139604 Hi there. Where are you travelling to please? Sorry for the cancellations this evening. Rachel
GWRHelp: @790959 Hi, this will be from next year as more new trains are delivered and replace the High Speed Trains. -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp @426690 @272023 Similar ones will be nearer to home on the East Coast soon. I am always willing to give new trains a chance.
GWRHelp: @562174 @790958 Hi there. Sorry to hear you missed this serviced. Were you able to catch the 1733 service to Newbury from Paddington? Rachel
Customer: @GWRHelp @360970 Next year is pretty vague - in the summer you said from October- when next year please?  Is that January or December - 17:36 and 17:49 cancelled to Maidenhead this evening!
Customer: @GWRHelp Maidenhead.
Customer: @GWRHelp Yes, but that's not really the point is it...?
Customer: @GWRHelp I’d be grateful if you focussed on getting the trains on the network and keeping us informed about that. New trains are useless if they are still being built or running empty on the tracks.  It’s hard to get excited about these trains when there aren’t any on my services or route
Customer: @GWRHelp Next year?  So is that in 6 weeks time?
GWRHelp: @139604 The 17:36 was cancelled due to a fault and 17:49 because of a broken down train earlier. Apologies for this and for any problems they have caused. Lewis
Customer: @GWRHelp Define 'demand'? I'm sure I'm not the only one who would have preferred not to nearly double journey time home!
GWRHelp: @790959 There will be additional electric commuter trains introduced in January. The IET introduction for serving Maidehead is yet to be confirmed but it will be early 2018  - Josh
Customer: @GWRHelp ... not even confirmed yet - so stop dangling the fruit in front of us if we can’t have it!  Marketing is about matching expectations and reality.
Customer: @GWRHelp Yup, and the 17:42 Pad-Mai jammed full of people you displaced and crawling.  At least extra stops weren’t added today.  But my question is about the rumour you have sold older rolling stock to Scot rail and not repairing broken down units. True or fake news?
Customer: @GWRHelp @426690 @272023 And then chucked in the bin.
Customer: @139604 @GWRHelp Not something I've heard, but GwR haven't sold anything...the HSTs that have gone to Scotland are off lease and don't belong to GWR . Vast majority have to go back as they are replaced by IETs and need to be given back in working order so last point makes no sense
GWRHelp: @790958 Decisions are taken with the route as a whole in mind as this delays the least amount of people overall. If demand is high and it doesn't delay a greater number, it will always been considered. Lewis
Customer: @275743 @GWRHelp But Dauntsey will be electrified so  why is this an issue? It was only two years ago that these didbt have any diesel capability at all!
Customer: @790970 @GWRHelp If that’s true then I wonder why so many units out of service? Have heard another explanation of a broken lathe.  That might be speculation but fact is lots of units out of service.
Customer: @GWRHelp Well the lesser number of us are crammed onto the 1812 from Reading like sardines, about to pick up all the fare dodgers from Reading West
Customer: @790972 @GWRHelp Actually pretty key - faster journeys allow more trains on the track, more frequent trains and therefore more seats.
GWRHelp: @790959 The IET introduction is confirmed but a specific date isn't yet - Josh
Customer: @GWRHelp Pity you’ve caused such huge chaos today at Paddington by cancelling the Hereford train for no good reason.
Customer: @GWRHelp and it appears this is not the first trains to be cancelled today. No reasons given so we can just assume it is just background incompetence.
Customer: @790970 @GWRHelp How many more services are there going to be between Cornwall and London?
GWRHelp: @306278 Hello. The service to Hereford was cancelled due to an earlier broken down train. Sorry for any inconvenience caused. Rachel
Customer: @GWRHelp @790966 Will there be hot food available? Or will it just be limited bits and pieces? Trolley service doesn't sound great - as the tea is usually not hot!
Customer: @GWRHelp @790972 Thats not actually fully correct. The HSTs used to do these trips much quicker in the 1980's as 2+7s and were slowed down over the years.
Customer: @GWRHelp @790966 Trolley service means no service on busy trains as they won’t be able to get through.
Customer: @GWRHelp @790966 😞😞😞😞 There goes our view, as I’ve heard that not all the seats will have a window, but the frame work due to the number of seats being crammed in.
Customer: @GWRHelp @790972 How much quicker is it compared to when GWR ran steam trains from Pad - Pen ?
Customer: @GWRHelp Hopeless.
GWRHelp: @303964 @790966 Hi Philip. They have a kitchen on-board and hot and cold food is available via an at seat service. Lewis
Customer: @GWRHelp @790966 Sounds good to me!
Customer: @320096 @GWRHelp Unfortunately it's about as comfortable as sitting on a concrete floor and none of the amenities function properly.
Customer: @GWRHelp Brave putting that up - predicable response from those who use your service day in day out. When do the timetable get updated to reflect reduce journey times ?
GWRHelp: @137808 Hi there. Improved journey times will be realised once all IET's are in service, this is scheduled for early 2019  - Josh
GWRHelp: @140344 @320096 Hi there. Sorry you feel like this Drew. The seats are ergonomically designed with extra leg room. Can you elaborate on the amenities not functioning please? - Josh
Customer: @790970 @GWRHelp I felt it was misleading of GWR to be boasting about their new trains’ acceleration when they are lacking in top end speed on diesel. They will be operating on plenty of unwired tracks for a long time to come.
Customer: @790967 @GWRHelp @790966 No different to the HSTs in that respect.
Customer: @GWRHelp The video of the IET looks sped up. The HST’s shrunk journey times when introduced in 1976. So what are the IET’s gonna do differently?
Customer: @275743 @GWRHelp Let's see them get up the South Devon banks
Customer: @GWRHelp 10 car IEP with less standard seats than 8 car HST & no through corridors betw units.5 or 9 cars will replace 8 car HST so much less capacity for Exeter.Engine can't hit 125 on diesel and MUCH slower uphill.16 min saving to Penzance down to reduced dwell & reduced recovery mainly
GWRHelp: @385920 Hi Heith. The IET's will also cut journey times. Once they are all introduced a journey from London Paddington to Bristol Temple Meads will be up to 17 minutes quicker. Lewis
GWRHelp: @274902 Hi KD. These new trains have up to 24% more seating than the current HST's. In ten carriage configurations they have 652 seats (580 in standard). The 802's when introduced in the summer can run with 5,9 or 10 carriages. Lewis
Customer: @GWRHelp The most uncomfortable seats in recent railway history won't make amends for an ever so slightly quicker acceleration time. And your own buffet staff are dreading trying to push a trolley over suitcases and bodies sitting on the floor due to overcrowding.
Customer: @GWRHelp @274902 Kd you stick to your Hst's then, this isn't the same train that will Go to the south west and beyond, thats a class 801 not an 802
GWRHelp: @711365 Hi there. Sorry you feel like this. Our new seats are ergonomically designed and have improved leg room. Our research showed that customers preferred the ease of an at seat trolley service - Josh
Customer: @GWRHelp Can you explain " ergonomically designed" please? Is it management speak for ' bolt upright' ? Thanks
Customer: @GWRHelp So long as there are enough carriages for the ticket paying customers I don’t care how long it takes to be honest. Window dressing doesn’t disguise poor service especially on local stopping commuter routes.
Customer: @GWRHelp When will we see them in the SW please?
GWRHelp: @534791 Hi Amanda. Apologies for any recent issues you've experienced. The IET's have increased capacity. Which route do you travel on please? - Josh
GWRHelp: @794915 Hi there. The IET's have been running to and from Bristol Temple Meads since October. More are being introduced on a phased basis - Josh
Customer: @GWRHelp When will we see them padd to Pen?
GWRHelp: @794915 They will be running to Penzance from Summer 2018 Ian - Josh
Customer: @306278 @GWRHelp Speaking from the Worcester/Hereford end, we’re used to being the @GWRHelp poor relations. Old trains, single track, expensive fares. I avoid GWR when possible and go @140497 to London.
Customer: @GWRHelp Why have two 5-car trains, with two sets of catering staff?  Wouldn't it make more sense to have one 10-car train?  You'd save money on two sets of cabs, and one set of catering crew!  5-car trains seem a bit short sighted to me!
GWRHelp: @794912 Hi there. The trains will be used as both 5 carriage and 10 carriage trains once all IET's are in service. The versatility is a huge plus of the train  - Josh
Customer: @775858 @GWRHelp Interesting, why were they slowed down?
Customer: @524048 @484651 @GWRHelp Most Portsmouth services WILL be 5 car from around late 2018
Customer: @306278 @GWRHelp Trains sometimes fail. It is a fact of life!
Customer: @GWRHelp @790960 And quicker still if it didn't have to lug a Diesel engine on a fully electrified line?
Customer: @792337 @524048 @GWRHelp Hst sets? Or still using 158/150s ?
GWRHelp: @484651 @792337 @524048 Morning Andrew. We're using Class 158 trains mainly between Cardiff Central and Portsmouth Harbour. In Summer 2018, Turbo Trains will be introduced. - Jordan
Customer: @GWRHelp Can’t get excited about this until you get the basics right because the reality is most GWR trains I take are late. One left on time recently...but was terminated with no explanation half way through the journey late at night.
GWRHelp: @237336 Which service are you referring to, Luisa? - Jordan
Customer: @GWRHelp Of course it doesn’t help if they are late arriving at Chippenham every morning!  Can you also confirm when seat reservations are actually going to work? Pointless my having a reserved seat if it’s not available.
GWRHelp: @130660 Sorry for the delay this morning, Michael. This was due to following a late running freight train. Seat reservations are live today. - Jordan
Customer: @GWRHelp That’s great, now that the trains are faster we reduce the number of daily services right? #GWR
Customer: @790972 @GWRHelp Driver quote yesterday on a forum: - Followed an iep today from Wooton Bassett to paddington , continually catching it up, it certainly was no match for the performance of my 2 + 7 HST. The future indeed ....
Customer: @GWRHelp I've heard the new trains don't serve hot food, is that correct?
Customer: @790972 @GWRHelp https://t.co/8wJq9Ar8zG
RMT are right for a change!
GWRHelp: @799486 Hello Tom. The new trains have a selection of hot food and drinks aboard! - Jordan
Customer: @GWRHelp @790958  https://t.co/pIvEbS6gzn
Customer: @775858 @790972 @GWRHelp Did you actually read the whole article or just assume from the headline?
Customer: @775858 @GWRHelp @790972 They also regularly used to speed well over the linespeed of 125mph until ATP stopped that.
Customer: @GWRHelp @274902 Not rocket science to work it out. Hst has either 7 or 8 carriages. You said a 10 car class800, now am a bit thick but, 10 is more than 7 or 8, bound to be more seats. Dear me,
Customer: @GWRHelp @145773 Does this mean until the fleet is fully in the new trains will have more dwell times in stations?
GWRHelp: @799842 @145773 Hello Rob. The new trains will reduce the dispatch time at stations and will reduce the journey time. - Jordan
GWRHelp: @244054 Hi Will, from 2019 we will have more trains running as faster trains allow us to run more services per day. -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp Hi GWR - can you explain how long Paddington to Swansea service will take when new rolling stock rolls put the yard in 2019?
Customer: @GWRHelp @145773 Oh noooo... you’ve designed brand new trains but still have to couple two together? That’s a logistical nightmare for most!
GWRHelp: @800155 @145773 Hi Joe, the five car units allow us greater flexibility in the fleet and mean we can split some of the less busy trains mid journey. This is a huge plus and allows us to run even more trains than we do currently. -Andy
GWRHelp: @800353 Hi Stewart, will save 17 minutes from 2019 allowing us to run more trains per day. -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp It's already been proven that the new trains won't be any quicker than the current HSTs. Also less flexibility as they are units. Less practical for staff and unless staff are in both sets less secure for passengers.
Customer: @GWRHelp When will these be in use on the Hereford-London route? Ta
GWRHelp: @263907 Hello James. The new trains offer faster journey times and five car sets give us more flexibility. There will be staff in both sets when the trains are joined together. - Jordan
GWRHelp: @422451 Hi Pete, this will start later this year/early next year. -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp Simple railway economics. Units are better on short stopping services. Loco hauled better on IC services. That's why almost every country in the world still uses loco hauled on IC services. Don't believe your own publicity.
Customer: @GWRHelp Yeah but, last time I checked, they can only do 100mph on diesel though. And given how much of the electrification project has been canned by DafT, acceleration improvements won’t offset the loss of top speed on an inter-city journey.
Customer: @GWRHelp That’s great but when are you actually going to introduce a Service for your customers and not just one to satisfy GWR? It has been woefully inadequate in recent weeks, especially at weekends. Despite many complaints to you, no replies as you prefer to hide behind bureaucracy!
GWRHelp: @800527 The new Intercity Express Train does 125 mph on diesel. Please see the photo here aboard our first train: https://t.co/AUIeNnqtBl - Jordan
Customer: @GWRHelp Hi Andy thanks for your answer , so that so how long in hours and minutes will it take?
GWRHelp: @128097 Hi Dan. What service are you referring to please? Also, are you referring to your tweets not getting a reply or emails? Rachel
GWRHelp: @800353 About 2 hours 45 minutes. -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp Rachel, I suggest you refer to my many tweets over last few weeks. You don’t actually deal with real issues but block customers from trying to make positive suggestions and get constructive responses. I don’t have to use GWR anymore so really couldn’t care but rate GWR CS as 4/10
Customer: @GWRHelp Is that all services or selected Andy?
GWRHelp: @800353 This is the fastest journey time on selected services. Some may take longer which make more stops. - Jordan
Customer: @GWRHelp Hi Jordan, which are the selected services? was is the normal operating service time from 7am to 7pm?
GWRHelp: @800353 The timetable hasn't been finalised yet for 2019. More details will be available nearer the time. - Jordan
Customer: @GWRHelp Would it not be good then not to advertise faster times and services until full details are to hand,  before spouting off what a great job GWR are doing bringing new rolling stock on board, when we do not know yet what we are actually getting? No disrespect you Jordan.
GWRHelp: @800353 The quoted journey time savings are correct, we do know what we are getting. The actual confirmed timetable just isn't available yet, but we can be certain when we talk about the journey time savings on fastest trains. -Andy
Customer: @790958 @GWRHelp Could be worse there. For instance, the time the "Cornish Riviera Express" was sent the wrong way: loco and five carriages of the Penzance train off down the branch to Henley before it came to a halt. ⚓️😡
Customer: @GWRHelp if you give an average journey time on all services from Paddington-Swansea in the last 6-12months,your customer base could really see what value they are receiving from https://t.co/Hvp1DrkSOi will fin forValue,comfort,reliability things need to change to hit the track running.
Customer: @GWRHelp @794915 What will be the journey time saved on a paddington to penzance service?
GWRHelp: @794916 @794915 Hi. Journey times between London Paddington and Penzance will be up to 16 minutes faster. Lewis
Customer: @GWRHelp @303964 @790966 Still prefer the buffet car. Hot food when you want it.
Customer: @GWRHelp Ooh. I’m happy to stand corrected then! I’m sure I’d read several articles that the class 800 would only manage 100mph on diesel (a shortcoming addressed in the 802) but prior to electrification cuts it wouldn’t have mattered. Oh well, yay 125mph!
Customer: @GWRHelp Which other train companys are getting the IET?
GWRHelp: @802457 Hi Finley. Just us. :) #GWRNewTrains Rachel
Customer: @GWRHelp Hi Rachel, I was just wondering because I saw virgin with the 801
Customer: @GWRHelp Where you have 2 five car sets joined do you have full first class catering service in both units
GWRHelp: @803085 Hello, yes that's correct there will be catering staff in both units. -Andy
GWRHelp: @802457 Yes but they are calling them something else! Same class of train of course but only GWR get the IET if you get my drift #GWRNewTrains -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp And when will exeter see electrification or even some new trains? #forgottensouthwest
GWRHelp: @803753 Hi there. Our new IET's will run to Exeter from summer 2018 - Josh
Customer: @GWRHelp First significant I provment in decades. Any sign of electrification or is tgat just for London?
Customer: @GWRHelp noticeable difference here! Impressive. As much as I'll miss the HST from growing up with it I'm excited for the IET #GWRNewTrains
GWRHelp: @378324 Glad you like it Ryan. Thanks for the lovely feedback! We look forward to welcoming you onboard our IETs. #GWRNewTrains Rachel
Customer: @GWRHelp @711365 You are just making trains faster by stripping out comfort, reducing luggage space and removing the heavy buffet car.
Customer: @794482 @GWRHelp @711365 That’s not entirely true. They have also added more first class carriages as these can remain empty which also helps with speed improvements.
Customer: @GWRHelp Very much looking forward to my first ride on one of these bad boys! Are they going to Cardiff and Swansea yet?
Customer: @153784 @794482 @GWRHelp Oh wonderful. More First Class, just what the tens of thousands of Standard Class passengers want to hear!!
GWRHelp: @134105 Hi Paul. They operate some services between Cardiff and Swansea but not all at present. Lewis
Customer: @GWRHelp Will the Bristol - Weymouth line get any love? 2 carriages every 2 and a half hours is not nearly enough for people travelling beyond Westbury...
GWRHelp: @503252 Good morning. Thank you for your enquiry. One of the team will respond to you first thing in the morning. AndyD
Customer: @GWRHelp And this is a selling point is it @GWRHelp? One of the many great things about the HST is the smooth, steady acceleration. You don't want to feel G force on an Intercity train. Another mark against IET I'm afraid.
GWRHelp: @808992 Hello. We'll pick this up and respond fully later this morning. AndyD
GWRHelp: @503252 Hi Spritzer. Additional carriages will be coming to this route from early 2018. Phil.
GWRHelp: @808992 Thanks for your feedback Duncan. Whilst quicker, the acceleration is still quite smooth on an IET and is important in the reduction of journey times. Phil.
Customer: @GWRHelp @237336 Happy to volunteer one on Louisa’s behalf - the ‘wonder train’ is currently over 40 mins late (Chippenham to Bath ‘08:17’)
Customer: @GWRHelp @237336 Oh and for added clarity, the same train was 15 minutes late yesterday as had to perform an emergency stop outside the station...  (failed safety equipment)
Customer: @GWRHelp So what happened to 1C03 this morning ?
Customer: @GWRHelp These look amazing, I can't wait! Cos my train Bristol-Bridgwater is absolutely terrible in comparison. Yesterday's started off 20 mins late but ended up 35 mins late as it kept being stopped to let other trains go past. Will be gr8 when they come here ... when will that b pls?
GWRHelp: @812058 Hi Alan, sorry for the delay this was late from the depot then further delayed at Reading because of a slight technical fault. -Andy
GWRHelp: @295471 Hello, glad you like the new trains! There will be some IETs on that route on the Paddington to Taunton direct services via Bristol but you will also get 4 car High Speed Trains between Cardiff and Taunton in the next few months. -Andy
Customer: @GWRHelp Good news, cheers! So the IETs will stop at Bridgwater then?
GWRHelp: @295471 Yes certain IET's will stop at Bridgwater. Rachel
Customer: @GWRHelp Thanks Andy , though after having the new trains for 2 years I would have expected them to have all the “slight faults” ironed out
Customer: @GWRHelp Poor service. Empty train with no bikes but as no reservation not allowed on board for the one stop Newport to Cardiff. Never mind, will now drive next week to Portsmouth instead of taking your train. Customer choice :-)
Customer: @GWRHelp Now stuck outside Cardiff waiting for your late running fancy new virtually empty train to get out the way. I'm now at risk of missing my connection. If only common sense was a requirement for your 'ttain managers'.
GWRHelp: @814395 Hi there. What connection are you looking to make? Rachel
Customer: @GWRHelp @503252 Bristol-Weymouth is my line, I suspect that some other trains will be cascaded down as part of an improvement. I had also hoped some HST's could appear on the Southampton-Cardiff service for all the cruise passengers!
Customer: @426690 @GWRHelp @274902 The carriages on the new trains are longer than the HST carriages so each one has more seats anyway. Which explains why some stations (like Bristol Parkway) are being extended.
Customer: @298956 @GWRHelp @274902 I have no issues with new trains and updating the fleets, longer carriages, more seats, that's good.
Customer: @298956 @426690 @GWRHelp Except that a 10 car IEP loses seats from the first& last coaches of each 5 due to engines which is why seat diff is not that much. Also they replace 8 car 125s with 5 car IEPs to PNZ which will have less seats&it won't be long before 5 car short forms to BRI show up too.
Customer: @298956 @426690 @GWRHelp Journey times are only speeding up as they are removing the recovery time they added in. The journey time compared to a decade or so ago will ve slower so hardly an improvement and seats are awful.
Customer: @274902 @298956 @GWRHelp I said along time ago when I saw a load of 5 cars being built, ya can't fit 7/8 carriages worth of punters into a 5 carriage unit.
Customer: @426690 @298956 @GWRHelp You can by claiming you'll run 10 when you know half the time you won't.Look at SWR  & shortforms of 5 vice 10 since First took over & also the consistent short forms on Bristol to Weymouth & Portsmouth causing severe overcrowding.5 was extremely shortsighted & very First Group.
Customer: @426690 @274902 @298956 @GWRHelp WTF are you on about, mate? We do that shit minimum daily. I love it when we cram double capacity on trains. Double the profits! I'm laughing to the bank at your expense! Haha sucker!
Customer: @274902 @298956 @GWRHelp Cross Country services used to be hsts yrs ago, 7 carriages, to be replaced by the  horrid voygers, which are far to short, always have been. I see constant overcrowding on the XC svcs regularly. FGW will be the same with the class800s
Customer: @GWRHelp Youv'e been promising them long enough....ans charging enough so when will we see them from Paddington to Hereford?
GWRHelp: @429108 Hi Craig. They will start to be introduced on the Hereford line from next month - Josh
Customer: @GWRHelp Looking forward to it. Thanks Josh.
Customer: @GWRHelp I'm afraid having ridden on your IET trains I cannot agree with you that their acceleration is smooth, one should not be able to feel the train accelerating. They are also noisey & rough riding in general. Faster journey times are not worth the sacrifice of having to use an IET
Customer: @GWRHelp I'm not afraid to say that GWR has allowed an inferior product on to the rails. If we must have these things thrust upon us then have the decency to lower your fares as compensation.
GWRHelp: @808992 Good morning. Thank you for your comments. One of the team will respond to you first thing in the morning. AndyD
Customer: @GWRHelp 1/2 Also let's not forget that under diesel power IET is slower to 100mph than a HST. IET puts it's power down at low speed like a commuter train. Let's not forget the inferior hill climbing ability of IET with VTEC admitting that IET will be 10 minutes slower than a 2+9 HST over
Customer: @GWRHelp 2/2. the Highlands. If they're slower than a 2+9 Jumbo HST they're going to be even slower than your 2+7 and 2+8 standard HST. Don't think nobody has noticed the recovery time already slipped in West of Cardiff either. I'm not against new stock, I'm against inferiority.
